transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah… I guess what brings me in is that I’ve had this low feeling hanging around for a long time now. I still get up, I still do my routes, I still show up for my volunteer shifts and do what I’m supposed to do, but most days it feels like I’m just kind of moving through it all on autopilot.

It’s not like I’m falling apart in some obvious way, I don’t think. From the outside I probably look like I’m managing. But inside it’s just this heavy, flat kind of feeling, like I’m not really in my own life the way I used to be. I’m getting things done, but I don’t feel very present in any of it. That’s probably the best way I can explain it.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, honestly. I mean, I still do some of the same things I used to do, and I can’t say I never enjoy anything at all, but it’s harder for me to tell what “pleasure” is supposed to feel like anymore, if that makes sense.

Like, I’ll go through the motions with things, and sometimes I’ll think, okay, that was fine, or I’m glad I did it instead of just sitting around. But it’s not always that same kind of easy enjoyment I remember having before. I guess I haven’t really sat down and measured it, you know? It’s more like I notice after the fact that things feel kind of muted. But I don’t know if I’d say I’ve completely lost interest or anything that clear-cut.
How long have you been experiencing this low feeling?

It’s been… about three years, I’d say. It started after my father died, or at least that’s when I first really noticed it settling in.

At the time I thought, well, of course I feel bad, you know? That made sense. I figured it was just part of dealing with him being gone, and that it would lift after a while. But it didn’t really lift. It just sort of stayed there in the background, and then over time it became hard to tell where the grief ended and where this ongoing low mood began. So, yeah… roughly three years now.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?

I guess I’m still not sure I’d call it “lost interest,” exactly. I haven’t stopped doing everything I used to do, and there are still moments where something feels okay or worthwhile. It’s more like the feeling I get from things is dulled down.

Like, if I do something I used to enjoy, I might still show up and participate, and afterward I can say, “Yeah, that was fine,” but I don’t always have that same pull toward it or that easy enjoyment while I’m doing it. Sometimes I’m doing it because it’s part of my routine, or because I know it’s probably better than doing nothing, rather than because I’m really looking forward to it.

So… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I have zero interest, but it doesn’t feel the same as it used to. It’s kind of muted, I guess.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past three years?

Not that I’ve clearly noticed, no. I mean, my weight probably goes up and down a little like anyone’s does, depending on what I’m eating or how busy I am with work, but I can’t point to some major change over the last three years.

I haven’t had to buy a whole different size of clothes or anything like that, and nobody’s really commented on it to me. I don’t weigh myself all the time, so I couldn’t give you an exact number, but from what I can tell, it’s been more or less the same.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns over the past three years?

Yeah, I have noticed that some, especially around work. It’s not every single night, but on nights before I’ve got a run the next day, I’ll get into bed and then my mind starts going over all the stops, what time I need to be where, whether traffic’s going to be bad, whether I’m forgetting something… just all that stuff.

Sometimes I do fall asleep eventually, but then I’ll wake up around four in the morning, maybe even a little before, and once I’m awake it’s like my brain turns back on. I might still lie there for another hour or two, but I’m not really sleeping again. I’m just kind of watching the clock and thinking, well, if I fall asleep now I’ll get this much time, and then that makes it worse.

I still usually make it to work on time, so from the outside it probably looks like I’m managing it okay. But those mornings, I feel like I’m already starting the day worn down before I’ve even gotten in the truck.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that you used to find enjoyable?

I don’t think I’d say I’m completely unable to feel pleasure, no. That sounds a little too absolute for what it’s like for me.

It’s more that it takes more for something to feel enjoyable, or the enjoyment doesn’t last as long. Like I can still have moments where I laugh at something, or I’m glad I did something instead of just sitting around. But a lot of the time, things I used to look forward to feel more like… I don’t know, just something to get through, or something I do because I know I should.

So if you mean, do I never enjoy anything anymore, then no, that’s not exactly it. But if you mean whether the enjoyment feels kind of weaker or harder to get to than it used to, then yeah, I guess that’s closer.
Have you had any thoughts about death or dying over the past three years?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I know everybody thinks about death once in a while, especially getting older—you hear about someone getting sick, or there’s an accident on the road, that kind of thing, and it crosses your mind.

But if you mean have I been sitting around thinking about dying a lot, or feeling like I want to die, I don’t think so. Nothing like a plan or anything like that. I wouldn’t say that’s been a regular thing for me.

Sometimes I might have a passing thought like, “What’s the point of all this?” when I’m really worn out, but it’s more like frustration or being tired than actually wanting to be dead. I don’t know if that’s what you’re asking. So… no, not in a serious way, I guess.
Have you ever found yourself wishing you were dead when you're feeling really down?

I don’t think so… not in the sense of actually wishing I was dead. When I’m really down, I can get kind of fed up and think things like, “I’m tired of this,” or “I don’t want to deal with today,” but that’s different from wanting to be dead, at least in my mind.

It’s more like wanting everything to stop for a while, or wanting a break from feeling worn out. I know that might sound close, but it doesn’t feel like I’m picturing death or hoping for it. I’m usually just frustrated, tired, and maybe feeling like I don’t have much left in the tank that day.

So… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve found myself wishing I were dead. More like wishing I could shut everything off for a bit and not have to think.
Have you ever had thoughts of harming yourself?

No… I don’t think I have. Not harming myself, like actually doing something to myself or thinking through how I would do it. That’s not really where my mind goes.

I can get pretty low and worn out, and sometimes I’m angry at myself or frustrated, but I haven’t had thoughts like, “I should hurt myself,” or anything like that. I don’t keep anything in mind or have some plan tucked away. It’s more just feeling overwhelmed and wanting the day to be over, if that makes sense.

So, no, I wouldn’t say I’ve had thoughts of harming myself.
Do you feel like things you used to enjoy are now completely unenjoyable to you?

Completely unenjoyable? I don’t know if I’d put it that strongly. I mean, there are definitely times where I don’t get as much out of things as I think I used to, or I kind of have to push myself to get going, but “completely” makes it sound like there’s just nothing there at all.

I still can enjoy things sometimes, at least a little. It might take me longer to settle into it, or I might not be as excited beforehand as I used to be, but once I’m doing something familiar or something easy, I can still get some enjoyment out of it. It’s not like everything has gone flat all the time.

So… no, I wouldn’t say things I used to enjoy are now completely unenjoyable. Maybe less enjoyable at times, but not completely gone.
Have you had more than one period of significant depression in the past three years?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it separate “periods” exactly, because it hasn’t felt like it cleanly came and went. It’s more like this whole thing has been going on for about three years now, really since my father died.

There have been stretches where it feels heavier and stretches where I’m functioning better, but it’s kind of been hanging around in the background that whole time. So if you mean, have I had more than one episode where I dropped down and then came back up completely and then dropped again, I’m not sure I’d describe it that way. But the depression, or whatever you want to call it, has been there in some form for about three years.
Have you had times in the past three years where you felt significantly better for a while, before feeling depressed again?

Not really in the sense of feeling “back to normal” for a while. It’s been more… uneven, I guess. This has been going on for about three years, since my father died, and there have been better days or better stretches, sure, where I’m getting through work and handling things and maybe not feeling it as strongly.

But I don’t remember a time in those three years where I thought, “Okay, that’s over, I feel like myself again,” and then later it came back. It’s more like it’s stayed around in the background the whole time, sometimes quieter and sometimes heavier. So I’ve had times that were somewhat better, but not really a clear break from it.
Have you had two or more distinct periods where you felt depressed, with some period of feeling normal in between?

I don’t think so, not like that. I know I keep circling around it, but it’s hard to separate it into neat chunks. It’s been going on for about three years, since my father died, and I can’t really point to a period in the middle where I felt normal again and then later got depressed again.

There have been ups and downs, sure, but not two clear, separate periods with a normal stretch in between. It’s more like the same thing has been there the whole time, just stronger sometimes and quieter other times.
Have you had periods where you felt completely better, without any depression, that lasted for at least a couple of months at any point in the past three years?

No, I don’t think I’ve had a couple of months where it was just completely gone. I’ve had better stretches, like I said, where I could get through the day and maybe it wasn’t sitting on me so hard, but I wouldn’t say I was completely better.

This has pretty much been going on for about three years, since my father died. It’s not always the same level every day, but I can’t point to any two-month stretch where I felt totally normal and free of it.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months where you felt completely free of depression since your father died?

No, I really don’t think so. Since my father died, this has just kind of been going on the whole time — about three years now. There might’ve been days or even little stretches where I was managing better, where I wasn’t thinking about it every minute, but I can’t say there was ever a full two months where I felt completely free of it. It’s more like it’s been there in the background the whole time.
Have you ever had a period of significant improvement where you felt like your old self again, even if it didn't last?

Not really like my old self, no. I’ve had times where I was doing a little better, or I could sort of get through things and maybe seem more normal from the outside, but I don’t think I ever felt like I was back to who I was before.

It’s been about three years now, since my father died, and it’s like there’s been this line before that and after that. Even during the better patches, I still knew it was there. So I wouldn’t say I had a real period where I felt fully like myself again, even if it didn’t last.
Have you felt like you've had a continuous low mood for the entire three years since your father died, without any breaks or significant improvements?

Yeah… I’d say that’s pretty much right. I don’t mean every single minute is exactly the same, because I can still do what I have to do — I get through my driving routes, I show up for my volunteer shifts, I talk to people when I need to. From the outside it probably looks like I’m functioning okay.

But underneath it, most days there’s this heavy, low feeling sitting on me. It’s like I’m moving through the day because I’m supposed to, not because I really feel present in my own life. There have been lighter days, sure, but not really a break where I thought, “Okay, I’m myself again.” It’s more like I’ve just been going through the motions for a long time.
Have you ever had a period of two weeks or more where you felt depressed nearly every day?

Yes… definitely. I mean, it’s hard for me to separate it into neat blocks of time, because it hasn’t felt like something that comes for two weeks and then leaves. It’s more like it’s been sitting there most days for a long time.

That’s kind of why I came in. I’m still getting through my routes, and I still go to my volunteer shifts, so I know from the outside it might not look like I’m falling apart. But inside, most days there’s this heavy, low feeling, like I’m just moving through what I’m supposed to do instead of really being in my own life. So yes, there have been plenty of stretches longer than two weeks where I’ve felt depressed nearly every day.
Have you had any periods where your depression seemed to completely resolve before returning?

No, I don’t think it ever completely went away and then came back. It’s more like… since my father died, about three years ago, it’s just been there in one form or another.

I’ve had days that were a little easier, or times where I could keep myself busy and not think about it as much, but I wouldn’t call that resolving. It wasn’t like I woke up and felt clear again, or felt like everything had lifted, and then later it returned. It’s been more continuous than that, just kind of changing in intensity but never really gone.
